description: We are a group searching for team members ready to win, challenge themselves, and have a good time. If this is you, welcome to the team!
summary: MarsBound is an interactive, multiplayer space mission design game that transforms complex aerospace engineering into an accessible, collaborative learning experience. Players become members of a space exploration team tasked with designing a Mars rover mission to investigate the planet's mineral composition, regolith (loose surface material), environmental conditions, and resources relevant to future human settlement.
details:
MARSBOUND is an educational, browser-based Mars mission-design simulator that introduces players to the challenges of planning and operating a Mars surface mission. Through an interactive, guided experience, participants define scientific objectives, design a rover, manage mission resources, respond to operational challenges, and evaluate their mission's results.

The gameplay follows a structured sequence, from the main menu and mission briefing through player roles, mission planning, rover design, mission control, and the Challenge Center, where players interact with Dr. Chen (Scientific Mentor) before reviewing their final mission evaluation.

Many people encounter space science through textbooks, videos, or simplified demonstrations without having the opportunity to experience the complex decision-making processes behind real space missions. MarsBound bridges this gap by transforming passive learning into an interactive experience where players become active problem-solvers, taking on the responsibilities of a collaborative Mars mission team.

MARSBOUND supports up to four local player slots within a single browser session; it does not feature online multiplayer. Its purpose is to make aerospace engineering concepts and mission-design trade-offs accessible through interactive gameplay, rather than serve as professional mission-planning or flight-engineering software.

Through gameplay, participants learn scientific terms, analytical reasoning, risk assessment, resource management, communication, and teamwork skills while gaining a better understanding of the challenges involved in space exploration.

In the long term, we envision MarsBound growing into an expandable educational platform featuring additional space missions, increasingly challenging scenarios, and simulations inspired by historical NASA missions, and even a rescue mission based on The Martian.

Our project aims to spark curiosity, encourage scientific thinking, and inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers by demonstrating an essential principle of space exploration: a successful mission is not simply about reaching another planet, but understanding how every decision contributes to achieving meaningful scientific results.
projectRefs: The Future of Space Exploration: Regolith
